column18: First assessment of winning tickets beyond accuracy (shift, uncertainty, interpretability, loss geometry); comparable performance at 20-99.53% sparsity
FPGA accelerator exploiting spatiotemporal spike sparsity: at least 17.5x lower prediction energy and 20x speedup vs state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators
Structural winning tickets via refill and regroup after IMP: up to 64.93%/64.84%/60.23% running time savings (CIFAR/Tiny-ImageNet/ImageNet)
Frame-camera ANN on embedded GPU vs event-camera SNN on event-based hardware, compared mainly on energy at similar accuracy; no figures
Sparse masks from an LTH variant composed for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer; outperforms adapters by a large margin; no efficiency figures
BERT winning ticket by dropping top-k layers: saves 78.1% time and 31.7% memory on average (up to 86.7% and 48%)
ANN-to-SNN conversion with double-threshold and augmented spikes on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10; compared only with other conversions; no ANN efficiency comparison
YOLOv3-tiny-to-SNN conversion for crater detection; mAP@0.5 0.396 at 128 time steps; no ANN efficiency comparison
SiamSNN tracker converted from Siamese networks; low energy and real-time on TrueNorth claimed; no ANN efficiency comparison
Proof that convolutional and residual networks with almost arbitrary activations contain lottery tickets with high probability; no efficiency figures
Correlation-based regularizer reduces redundant features and spike count with limited accuracy loss versus vanilla and rate-regularized SNNs; no figures
DL vs DL-to-SNN conversion on Loihi and Akida for network intrusion; power savings explored, results only called promising, no figures
ANNs sub-ms inference, sub-mm accuracy with 10^4-10^5 parameters; SNNs reasonably good with few thousand neurons; Xavier vs Loihi
Double-win matching subnetworks at up to 91.41% (CIFAR-10) and 83.22% (CIFAR-100) sparsity from adversarial pre-training; more data-efficient
SNN on Loihi consumed 95% less energy per inference than SOTA DNNs on Jetson TX2 with similar EEG classification performance
Phasor networks run as ANN or spiking without conversion; low-energy suitability asserted, no efficiency metrics or comparison
Residual SNN beats ANN counterpart in energy efficiency (no figure); 86.5K vs 210K footprint; accuracy +4 to 17% over SNN
LTH- and DSD-based pruning of small DenseNets at several granularities; DSD efficient at cutting parameters, best at individual-weight level
SpikeDHS on event-based deep stereo: higher accuracy than specially designed ANNs with 26x lower energy (6.7 mJ)
LTH sub-networks for languages and tasks are topologically similar (language-neutral) and give effective cross-lingual initializations; no efficiency figures
Multi-Ticket Ensemble: fine-tuned winning-ticket subnetworks of one pretrained model give more diverse predictions and beat standard ensembles on some tasks
Doge tickets: domain-general parameter subnetworks selected with a variance-based score improve out-of-domain generalization of pre-trained LMs; no efficiency figures
DLTH: random subnetworks transformed into trainable tickets by Random Sparse Network Transformation (regularization) match LTH; no efficiency figures
DynSNN dynamic pruning, co-activity inspired: ~0.3% accuracy loss at 34% compression (CIFAR, ImageNet), lossless 60% compression on MNIST
E-prop spiking RNN on SpiNNaker 2: 91.12% GSC, 680 KB; estimated 12x less energy than V100 GPU; no ANN comparison
